adobe.reason: Adobe's homepage and sign-in page both answer a headless browser with a near-blank bot-wall / consent interstitial instead of the real page. The capture is recognised as degenerate (fewer than 3% of pixels outside the modal colour) and rejected, so no layout or thumbnail reference is shipped for Adobe.
adobe.mitigation: scripts/data/generate_reference_hashes.ts retries each brand with a realistic browser identity (AutomationControlled disabled, en-US locale, persistent --user-data-dir profile so consent cookies are replayed). That is enough for most walls; Adobe's has not yielded. A capture from a real signed-in Chrome profile, or an operator-supplied reference, is the remaining path.
adobe.user_impact: None beyond a missing brand: the visual layer simply has no Adobe reference, the side-by-side view shows the captured page only, and every other signal (icon match, layout hash, URL, domain, LLM) still applies.
